incumbent.extractionIntent: Record the SHIPPED visual system as a post-P0 baseline so the redesign can treat it as evidence and anti-reference. Descriptive only. Nothing in this file is a target, a recommendation, or a direction to build toward.
incumbent.confirmedAntiReference: The incumbent world reads as generic technical SaaS — dark navy plus cyan, dot grid, gradient glow, repeated dark cards, and Inter throughout. Recorded 2026-08-16 per the redesign audit.

corroboration.source: Impeccable mechanical design detector, run over src/app/globals.css 2026-08-16
corroboration.establishes: Two independent methods applied to THIS codebase reached the same reading of it: the surface presents as generic rather than particular.
corroboration.doesNotEstablish: That Inter is a poor typeface, that dot-grid fields are bad generally, or that either must be removed. Both are defensible in a system that has a reason for them. Whether either survives is a decision for the redesign brief, resolved in `shape` against confirmed product truth — not settled by this baseline.
corroboration.disposition: Left unfixed and unsuppressed. No ignore rule added. Fixing would be a source change in a documentation-only capture; suppressing would delete evidence a later verification pass should be able to re-derive.

knownDefectsReproducedFaithfully: Component specimens use #94A3B8 for secondary text, matching what main now ships after PR #17. The former #64748B no longer appears in source.
No specimen defines a :focus-visible style, because the incumbent system defines none anywhere.
No specimen defines a prefers-reduced-motion override, because the incumbent system defines none.

Hover behaviour is reproduced as shipped: page-level CTAs have NO hover treatment; only the navigation CTA and navigation links change on hover, and they do so via inline JS event handlers rather than CSS pseudo-classes.
The availability badge dot uses animate-pulse with no reduced-motion guard.

narrative.metaphorNote: A reading of what shipped, not a direction to build toward. The redesign is not required to honor it and should not treat it as a brief.
narrative.overview:
Terra Pay X renders itself as instrumentation. The ground (#020817) is an unlit room; panels (#0D1426) are the surfaces that catch light; a dot-grid substrate sits beneath the hero at 40% opacity as the faint graph paper such rooms are built on. Against that near-monochrome darkness Signal Cyan is the visually dominant accent and often reads as the live channel, but the incumbent mapping is inconsistent: cyan also decorates, while teal also acts. Depth arrives largely as a response to attention: no surface carries a resting box-shadow, though the hero carries a permanent ambient glow.

The density is generous rather than packed: an 1152px reading column, 80-96px between sections, 32px inside feature panels. Type does almost all of the structural work, since the palette refuses to. Hierarchy is carried by weight and scale in a single family, with a wide-tracked uppercase micro-label doing the job that a second typeface would do in a warmer system.

The character this produces is precise, quiet, and slightly clinical — a system that would rather be trusted than liked. That is also its limitation, and it is recorded here deliberately.
narrative.antiReference: The incumbent world reads as generic technical SaaS — dark navy plus cyan, dot grid, gradient glow, repeated dark cards, and Inter throughout. Recorded 2026-08-16 per the redesign audit.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black navy ground with a single raised panel tone; no third surface level
Two accents and nothing else chromatic — but neither maps cleanly to interactivity: cyan is also decorative, and teal is simultaneously a state, a category marker, and a purchase action
No resting box-shadow anywhere; interactive surfaces gain glow and lift only on hover. The hero is the exception — it carries a permanent ambient glow
Hairline 1px borders used both as component outlines and as section/nav/footer dividers
One typeface carrying five roles through weight and scale alone
Wide-tracked uppercase micro-labels on eyebrows, though not on all small text

rules.name: The One Live Color Pattern
rules.body: Signal Cyan is the accent most often found on something actionable, and the palette is otherwise near-monochrome, so cyan does read as the page's live channel. It is NOT a reliable signal of interactivity in either direction. Cyan without interaction: capability-list icon strokes, the hero's permanent ambient glow, the card hover glow, the scrollbar thumb, and the oversized principle numerals at rgba(56,189,248,0.18). Interaction without cyan: the hero 'Get the Starter Kit' CTA is Confirmation Teal, ghost buttons are hairline-bordered with Read text, navigation links are Aside or Read.

rules.name: The Teal Ambiguity Defect
rules.body: Confirmation Teal carries three unrelated roles on main: resolved state (the 'Available today' badge and its pulsing dot, checkmark icons), division/category marking (divisionColor on Labs-owned entries), and action (the hero 'Get the Starter Kit' CTA, page.tsx:79). A visitor cannot learn what teal means because it does not mean one thing. Recorded as an incumbent defect, not a scheme.

rules.name: The Inverted Card Pattern
rules.body: Panels are lighter than the page, and cards placed on panels are usually filled with Ground — darker than their container. This is the majority pattern, not a rule: of the card surfaces on main, 8 use Ground and 4 use Panel.

rules.name: The Contrast Debt Rule
rules.body: RESOLVED 2026-08-16. The incumbent system carried #64748B at 4.20:1 on Ground and 3.85:1 on Panel, below WCAG AA, across 19 sites. PR #17 (2e455262) raised it to #94A3B8 (7.80:1 / 7.15:1) site-wide; #64748B now occurs 0 times. Retained as history so the current value reads as a correction, not an original choice.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Family Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight (400/500/600/700) and scale. The system uses exactly one family — though it loads that one family through two paths: next/font in layout.tsx and a Google Fonts @import in globals.css.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Label Pattern
rules.body: Section eyebrows and hero badges at 12px are uppercase, weight 500-600, tracked 0.1em-0.15em. This is NOT universal to 12px: of 91 text-xs uses on main, 45 are not uppercase.

rules.name: The No Reactive Glow At Rest Rule
rules.body: Interactive surfaces do not glow until touched — a card, badge, or button emitting light at rest is broken. This does not extend to the page: the hero's ambient glow is permanent and is part of the incumbent atmosphere, not a state.

dos: Do keep the palette near-monochrome, with accent coverage low — roughly 10% of any viewport. Note the incumbent system does NOT restrict Signal Cyan to actionable elements; see The One Live Color Pattern for counted exceptions.
Do carry hierarchy with weight and scale in Inter rather than reaching for a second family.
Do set section eyebrows as uppercase, weight 500-600, tracked 0.1em-0.15em — but do not extend that to all 12px text; badges and fine print are sentence case.
Do hold body copy to a max-w-2xl (672px) measure regardless of container width.
Do expect a card on a Panel section to be Ground-filled most of the time (8 of 12), while treating that as a tendency rather than a constraint.
donts: Don't introduce a resting box-shadow. Depth is tonal; reactive glow is a hover response.
Don't add a third surface tone. The system is Ground and Panel only.

Don't mix radii within a component family, or give a boxed action anything other than 8px. Radius is not a marker of clickability — navigation links, inline links and the wordmark are clickable with no radius, background or border.
remediationNotIncumbent: Add a :focus-visible treatment. The incumbent system has none anywhere.
Add a prefers-reduced-motion override, including for the animate-pulse availability dot.
Remove the Google Fonts @import from globals.css so Inter loads once.
Replace inline JS hover handlers on navigation with CSS pseudo-classes.
